problem: Does nonzero bright occupation suffice for two local coupling directions in the four-probe test?
bold_conjecture: Every positive bright density retains a nonsingular two-coupling contrast Jacobian at the declared source couplings.
rivals: Only zero bright occupation loses sensitivity
A non-dark positive density gives rank loss
A sampled rank loss is nonpositive or a frame/numerical artifact
source_operation: Contract the retained full effect derivatives with the retained contrast rows, then compress to the source ground matching support. No new source operator or parameter fit.
full_ground_witness: Half bright density plus half normalized dark projector, fixed across all four energies
determinant_form: det C(b)=d0+l dot b+b^T Q b; obtain coefficients algebraically from the affine2x2 Jacobian, not by curve fitting
witness_search: Evaluate center, six coordinate-axis endpoints, eight normalized cube vertices, and plus/minus eigenvectors of Q. If an endpoint changes sign relative to center, use the first such endpoint and bracket its radial root in[0,1]. Do not widen this search after observing results.
uniform_bound: abs(d0)-norm(l)-norm(Q,2)>0 is sufficient, not necessary, for all Bloch-ball determinants to stay nonzero
finite_checks: Polynomial versus direct operator determinant at the fixed states
Full ground density positivity and source-flux signal for any root witness
Passive two-dimensional Fourier bright-frame change transports density and preserves its Jacobian
